why: Both concern April Fools claims in the same room and turn only on whether the room itself staged the claim being played with or tested.

why.T3-001: The room's own moderator posts a one-line April Fools item inside the sub and commenters answer that specific fake with doubtful laughter and ribbing, i.e. staging and being caught in the room's own fake, not testing an outside or moderator-authority claim (T3-095) nor a sub-wide staged change (T3-023).

why.T3-097: The single code revisits the sub's April Fools state days later to ask whether it has been switched back, treating the prank rules/look as something to get past, not playing inside it (T3-023).

why.T3-005: Warnings that someone is destroying the Yak, a defensive design made to fight back, vigilance calls and a call to avenge are the attack-and-answer that T3-005 gates, not mere watching and fixing (T3-021).
why.T3-029: RIP memorials, mourning the hours spent and lament over the unrecognisable remains voice grief for the lost Yak, which T3-005's fight material does not reach.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-005's gate covers the attack on the Yak and the room's answer to it but not the RIP memorials and the voiced grief for the erased work.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: A RIP memorial and mourning the hours spent on the Yak are grief voiced for the lost work, T3-029's gate, carried by its own concept C0198893.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-029; if forced to one I would drop it and lose the grief and memorials for the lost Yak.

why.T3-070: White-border, location, mirror-plan, site and which-picture directions are circulated for placers to follow by hand, i.e. directions shared for use rather than one plan imposed against stray versions (T3-091) or a new mark proposed (T3-033).

why.T3-033: A member offers the room what to go for with a circulated new plan and 'This should be what we go for', an idea of what to make offered to the room, not the look of a chosen mark worked out (T3-004) or a spot chosen (T3-020).

why.T3-017: Both passages keep the sub's ordinary political subject going by pointing members to other Ontario venues, ordinary talk of the room's usual subject rather than a canvas or April Fools act.

why.T3-065: The work called for and started is the flag of the room's own land (Ontario), which T3-065 claims for the calls, the starting corner, the design link and the Canada-flag reference alike, not any other picture (T3-002) or a shared template (T3-070).

why.T3-009: 'Good job everyone', a valiant effort and excitement at the remnant mark the room's finished effort as achieved, celebration of the work rather than the canvas's end itself (T3-117) or a plain account of what happened (T3-073).

why.T3-010: Reframing griefing as shared space, negotiating with SquareSpiral, redirecting after a refusal and settling the r/eve overlap are lines and space settled with neighbours where no fight began, T3-010's gate.
why.T3-022: Seeking a new sanctuary, proposing another move and finding an abandoned new spot after the Yak was overrun are the work moved or restarted after loss, T3-022's gate.
why.T3-149: The Orange Blob asking for a truce after destroying the Yak and edBoxes offering peace talks are pacts ending or forestalling a fight between rooms in contact, T3-149's gate.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-010 settles lines and shared space with neighbours but does not reach the Yak's repeated relocations once its spot was erased or crowded out.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: Seeking a new sanctuary and finding an abandoned new spot after the old one was lost satisfy T3-022, carried by its own concept C1489228.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-022; dropping it would lose the repeated moves of the Yak.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-010 settles borders where no fight began and does not carry the truces asked of rooms that had already attacked the Yak.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: The Orange Blob's request for a truce after destroying the Yak and edBoxes' offer of peace talks satisfy T3-149, carried by its own concept C1245130.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-149; dropping it would lose the truces with former attackers.

why.T3-095: Members test the moderators' fake-rule announcement, check the calendar, admit being fooled and resubscribe, working out whether a claim they did not make is a joke, not playing inside a change they know (T3-023) nor judging an official maker's joke (T3-048).

why.T3-023: Members keep the staged sub-wide fake rules in play by testing their limits, mock-banning and promoting, performing approved praise and inventing flair and source rules, playing inside the sub's changed state for the day, not testing whether it is real (T3-095) or objecting to it (T3-032).

why.T3-038: Inviting the build and reporting its state (Yak complete, 'The Yak Lives!', 'The Yak is back!', three people building) is placing the mark and reporting its progress; the item also satisfies T3-002 (rallying hands to build, fix and pool efforts), T3-021 (repairing damage and maintaining the Yak) and T3-141 (night watches and overnight rebuilding), more than three themes, so it is recorded as a bag on T3-038.

why.T3-016: One code asks how r/place works after not understanding it and the other reports abandoning an appeal after refreshing a bugged canvas, i.e. encountering the event's mechanics, not directions for the room's own work (T3-070) nor the cooldown worked around while building (T3-074).

why.T3-017: Both passages keep the sub's ordinary political subject going by pointing members to other Ontario venues, ordinary talk of the room's usual subject rather than a canvas or April Fools act.

why.T3-023: The moderators announce a sub-wide fake rule change for April Fools, new rules, party flair, automod and a promised second set, staged by the sub's moderators, a change to the sub itself for the day (T3-023), not a member's fake post (T3-001) nor a claim being tested (T3-095).
